text.p: PRAVDA - The Central Referendum Committee on Monday declared the weekend referendum on NATO membership and direct presidential elections invalid since the plebiscite was carried out with invalid ballots containing only three NATO questions.
- Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik on Monday resigned from his post saying the domestic political situation and the failed weekend referendum had made his position untenable.
- Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar on Monday met all ambassadors accredited in Slovakia to discuss the referendum and related political issues.
- President Michal Kovac on Monday said Meciar and Interior Minister Gustav Krajci were responsible for the referendum failures by thwarting the plebiscites and called for both to resign.
- Kovac said Meciar was an obstacle for Slovakia's integration into western structures.

- Meciar's ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) on Monday accused President Kovac of deliberately preventing citizens from voting in the referednum on NATO membership by joining the plebiscite with a poll on direct presidential elections. HZDS called for Kovac to resign.
- Slovakia's major penicillin-based drug producer, Biotika, said it may seek a strong strategic partner to help it retain its good market position in Europe.
SME - President Kovac said he had no intention of resigning.

- The Central Referendum Committee said it had initiated legal actions against Krajci for thwarting the NATO and presidential referendums by distributing ballots without questions on presidential elections.
- European Union (EU) Commissioner Hans van den Broek will visit Bratislava on May 29 to prepare a report on development of democratic principles in Slovakia.

NARODNA OBRODA - The EU said the recent political development in Slovakia is not likely to result in withdrawal of the association agreement with Bratislava. But the union said chaos over the referendum can influence the European Commission's statement on Slovakia's readiness for EU membership.
- Local dealers said downward pressure on the crown eased significantly on Monday.

- Prime Miniser Vladimir Meciar said the government might administratively reduce imports of unspecified Czech foodstuffs in the near future if Slovakia's trade balance with the Czech Republic continues to show a negative trend.
- The government holds its regular session on Tuesday. The preliminary agenda does not include any major economic items.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Slovak commercial banks seem to prefer stability of the crown over short-term profits from downward pressure on the currency.
